program_name: Two names for one programme, and this must be handled carefully because the two universities label it differently. AT UNIBZ: 'International Master in Horticultural Science (IMaHS)' — this is the title of the unibz programme page and of the unibz brochure PDF; in unibz's own faculty and timetable listings it is shortened to just 'Horticultural Science' under the Faculty of Agricultural, Environmental and Food Sciences master programmes. AT THE UNIVERSITY OF BOLOGNA (the university you actually apply to): 'Second Cycle Degree/Two Year Master in International Horticultural Science', Italian 'Laurea Magistrale in International Horticultural Science', internal course codes 6784 (current ordinamento) and 8883 (previous ordinamento), abbreviated 'IMaHS' throughout unibo's own documents (e.g. the official 2026/27 admission notice is headed 'Admission notice to the Second Cycle Degree Programme in International Horticultural Science - ImaHS, LM-69 - Cod.6784'). In the unibo Studenti Online application portal the programme must be selected under the exact string 'INTERNATIONAL HORTICULTURAL SCIENCE - IMAHS'. It is a JOINT DEGREE: unibo states 'The second cycle degree programme in International Horticultural Science - IMaHS is a joint degree programme, in partnership with the Free University of Bozen' and 'The completion of the International Program issues a joint Degree recognized by both institutions'. Delivered by unibo's Department of Agricultural and Food Sciences (DISTAL) together with unibz's faculty in Bolzano.
level: Master — Italian 'laurea magistrale' / second-cycle degree, EQF level 7, 120 ECTS over 2 years (4 semesters of 30 ECTS each). Entry qualification is a first-cycle (bachelor) degree of at least 180 ECTS: unibo requires a 'first cycle Degree, or a three-year university Degree, or other qualification obtained abroad, recognised as equivalent' and, for foreign three-year degrees, 'a first cycle University Degree in Life Sciences (e.g., Horticulture, Agriculture, Biology) obtained upon achievement of at least 180 ECTS'. The degree gives access to Italian PhD programmes; unibz runs directly related doctorates in 'Mountain Environment and Agriculture' and 'Food Engineering and Biotechnology', and unibo/DISTAL runs agricultural PhDs.
teaching_language: FULLY ENGLISH-TAUGHT at both universities — this is NOT one of unibz's trilingual programmes and it is not an Italian-taught unibo programme either. unibo states the programme is 'Delivered entirely in English' and that 'the program is entirely taught and assessed in English'. unibz's page and brochure list the teaching language as English. CONSEQUENCES: (1) the ONLY language required for admission is English at CEFR B2; (2) there is NO German requirement and NO Italian requirement at entry or at graduation; (3) crucially for non-EU applicants, because the programme is taught in English the applicant is EXEMPT from unibo's Italian-language requirement — unibo's rule is that non-EU citizens residing abroad enrolling in Italian-taught programmes must prove Italian at B2 (unibo test min. 48/72, or CELI/CILS/PLIDA/CERTIT B2), and 'This requirement does not apply to students enrolling in English-taught programs'. PRACTICAL CAVEAT (not a curricular requirement): the first year is in Bologna, a monolingual Italian city where daily life, housing contracts, the questura and the AUSL health office all operate in Italian; the third semester is in Bolzano/Bozen, which is officially bilingual Italian/German and where German is the majority local language in the surrounding fruit- and wine-growing valleys. Neither affects the degree, but both affect internships and part-time work.
campus: THREE-PHASE GEOGRAPHY ACROSS TWO UNIVERSITIES AND TWO REGIONS — this is the defining feature of the programme and the single biggest logistical planning item. PHASE 1 — FIRST YEAR (semesters 1 and 2), BOLOGNA. unibo's 2026/27 course structure diagram states verbatim: 'all the courses of the First year will be offered exclusively at the University of Bologna (Agriculture Campus - Viale Fanin, 50 BOLOGNA - Italy)'. This is unibo's agriculture campus, home of DISTAL, in the south-east of Bologna city (Emilia-Romagna). PHASE 2 — SECOND YEAR, FIRST PERIOD = the programme's THIRD SEMESTER, BOLZANO. unibo states verbatim: 'the third semester will be offered exclusively at the Free University of Bolzano (Faculty of Science and Technology - Piazza Universita, 1 BOLZANO - Italy)'. Note the address given is unibz's main city-centre campus at Universitatsplatz 1 / piazza Universita 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano. [uncertain] unibo's diagram still names unibz's 'Faculty of Science and Technology'; unibz has since reorganised and now lists this programme under the Faculty of Agricultural, Environmental and Food Sciences, so the faculty label in the unibo text is stale even though the address is right. Some agricultural teaching and labs in Bolzano also take place at the NOI Techpark / Laimburg research-centre facilities, but the unibo diagram names only piazza Universita 1. PHASE 3 — SECOND YEAR, SECOND PERIOD = the FOURTH SEMESTER, FLEXIBLE. unibo states verbatim: 'Please note that the 2nd period there are not courses, students could choose to carry out their internship and the thesis research at both institutions or abroad.' So the final semester (internship + master thesis) can be spent in Bologna, in Bolzano, in industry, or abroad. ADDED MOBILITY: 'Students enrolled will have the opportunity to spend up to two semesters (2nd, 3rd or 4th) in one of the European partner universities as exchange students Erasmus+ (with financial assistance) and be entitled to earn a Double Degree in some cases.' Named Erasmus+ partners: Szent Istvan University of Budapest (Hungary), Technical University of Munich (Germany), BOKU Wien / University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences Vienna (Austria), Humboldt University of Berlin (Germany). PRACTICAL NOTE: Bologna and Bolzano are roughly 250 km apart (about 2.5-3 hours by direct Trenitalia regional/Frecciarossa services). Students therefore need TWO separate housing arrangements — the Emilia-Romagna student-welfare body ER.GO covers Bologna accommodation, while Bolzano housing is a separate South Tyrolean market and is notoriously tight and expensive. Budget and residence-permit address changes must be planned for the move.
degree_class: LM-69 — 'Scienze e tecnologie agrarie' (Agricultural Science and Technology), the Italian ministerial second-cycle degree class. unibo's programme pages for A.Y. 2026/27 give the class in the post-reform form 'LM-69 R - Agriculture' (the 'R' suffix marks the class as re-defined under the 2023/2024 ministerial reform, M.D. 1649/2023); the official 2026/27 admission notice writes it simply as 'LM-69 - Cod.6784'. Both refer to the same class — this resolves the 'to be verified' status the class carried in the source brief. unibo internal course codes: 6784 (current) and 8883 (older code still used in some scholarship calls, e.g. 'corso LM 8883 - International Horticultural Science'). CONSEQUENCES OF LM-69: (a) it is the standard Italian agronomy master class, so it maps to the Italian professional register of agronomists and foresters (Albo dei Dottori Agronomi e Dottori Forestali, section A) after the state exam; (b) under Italian law on simultaneous enrolment (Law 33/2022) a second simultaneous programme must not be in the same class; (c) it is a different class from unibz's own agricultural masters, so it does not overlap with them administratively.

majors_tracks_study_plans: NO MAJORS, NO TRACKS, NO CURRICULA — a single study plan for everyone, with a genuinely large elective and mobility component. There is one admission route and no track to choose at application. FIRST YEAR, BOLOGNA — 54 ECTS of compulsory courses plus 6 ECTS chosen from a restricted list, total 60. Compulsory: Academic Basecamp (3, soft skills: teamwork, problem solving, decision making, communication); Advanced Plant Pathology and Entomology (6, AGRI-05/B); Ecosystems and Plant Ecophysiology (6, AGRI-03/A); Horticultural Crop Yield and Quality (integrated course) = Crop Ecology and Crop Quality (6, AGRI-03/A) + Vegetable Crops (3, AGRI-02/B); Horticultural System Management and Economics (6, AGRI-01/A); Methods of Research and Analysis in the Horticulture System (integrated course) = Agricultural Policy Evaluation (3, AGRI-01/A) + Research Methods for Horticultural Business (6, AGRI-01/A); Scientific Method in Horticultural Research (3, AGRI-03/A); Soil Fertility and Plant Biochemistry (6, AGRI-06/B); Sustainable and Safe Use of Horticultural Equipment (6, AGRI-04/B). Restricted-choice 6 ECTS: either Crop Biotechnology (integrated) = Biotechnological Approach to Increase Sustainability (3, AGRI-03/A) + Biotechnology of Plant Probiotics (3, AGRI-08/A), or Innovative and Smart Technologies for Vegetable Cultivation (integrated) = Smart Horticulture (3, AGRI-02/B) + Urban Farming (3, AGRI-02/B). SECOND YEAR, THIRD SEMESTER AT UNIBZ IN BOLZANO — 26 ECTS compulsory: Internship (5, may be started from the first semester and may be done abroad); Post-Harvest Chain Management (integrated) = Fruit Processing (3, AGRI-07/A) + Post-Harvest Management (3, AGRI-05/B) + Supply/Value Chain and Innovation Management (3, AGRI-01/A); Production Chain Management (integrated) = Applied Entomology in Horticulture Crops (3, AGRI-05/A) + Mineral Nutrition (3, AGRI-06/B) + Orchard and Vineyard Management (6, AGRI-03/A). Plus 9-12 ECTS of free electives from two Bolzano integrated courses: Efficient Resource Use in Production Systems = Applied Breeding and Sustainability (3) + Information and DSS in Fruit Production (3) + Project Development and Management (3, IEGE-01/A); and Plant Protection and Disease Management = Elements of Chemistry and Biochemistry of Agrochemicals (3) + Integrated Plant Disease Management (3) + Plant Protection Products and Residues (3). SECOND YEAR, FOURTH SEMESTER — no courses; final-exam group of 13-25 ECTS with five alternative shapes: Original Experimental Thesis (25 ECTS) or Original Experimental Thesis (13 ECTS); Internship for Preparation of the Final Examination (12); Internship Abroad for Preparation of the Final Examination (12); Preparation for the Final Examination Abroad (12). Internship credits (5 ECTS) and thesis-internship credits (up to 12 ECTS) may be ANTICIPATED into the first year. DOUBLE-DEGREE OPTION (joined after enrolment, not at admission): up to two semesters (2nd, 3rd or 4th) at Szent Istvan University Budapest, TU Munich, BOKU Wien or Humboldt University Berlin as an Erasmus+ exchange student with financial assistance, 'and be entitled to earn a Double Degree in some cases'. [uncertain] The double-degree selection procedure, quotas, deadlines and any language requirements for the German/Hungarian/Austrian partners are not published on either the unibo or the unibz programme pages.
english_only_accessibility: OPEN — and, on the language axis alone, one of the most accessible Italian agricultural masters for an English-only candidate. WHY OPEN: (a) the sole language requirement is English at CEFR B2 ('English language skills are required to at least CEFR level B2'); (b) there is NO German, NO Italian, NO third-language and NO graduation-language requirement anywhere in the programme; (c) as an English-taught programme it is explicitly exempt from unibo's Italian B2 requirement that otherwise binds non-EU citizens residing abroad; (d) the whole application, the oral assessment interview and all documents are handled in English or Italian, with English fully sufficient; (e) admission is OPEN ACCESS, so no candidate is squeezed out by a place cap. WHAT ACTUALLY LIMITS ACCESS IS THE CURRICULAR FILTER, NOT LANGUAGE. The binding constraint is a life-sciences/agriculture bachelor, or failing that a minimum of 5 ECTS each in four very specific Italian subject groups (AGR/01 agricultural economics and rural appraisal, AGR/03 arboriculture and fruitculture, AGR/11 general and applied entomology, AGR/12 plant pathology). A candidate with a general biology, chemistry, environmental engineering or food-technology background can easily fail on the entomology and plant-pathology lines specifically, because those two are rarely compulsory outside an agronomy curriculum. THE SECOND FILTER IS THE ORAL EXAMINATION. Only candidates holding an Italian L-25/L-26 (or L-20 ex 509/99) degree with a final mark of at least 100/110 are exempt. In practice EVERY foreign-qualified candidate should expect to sit an online oral exam on agricultural economics and rural appraisal, arboriculture and fruitculture, general and applied entomology and plant pathology. That is a substantive technical hurdle conducted in English. THE THIRD FILTER FOR NON-EU APPLICANTS IS THE CALENDAR, NOT THE COMPETITION. Non-EU citizens residing abroad can only use Intakes 1 and 2 (closing 28/02/2026 and 10/05/2026 for the 2026/27 cycle); Intakes 3 and 4 are 'EU citizen applicants only'. Missing the May intake costs a full academic year. NET ASSESSMENT: language-open, curriculum-restrictive, calendar-critical. Rated OPEN, with the caveat that the openness is administrative rather than academic.
admission_type: OPEN ACCESS (accesso libero) WITH A COMPULSORY SUITABILITY CHECK — and the application is made to the UNIVERSITY OF BOLOGNA, NOT to unibz. THE MOST IMPORTANT SINGLE FACT: unibz's own page and brochure state verbatim 'You must apply to the University of Bologna.' unibz publishes NO admission information for this programme — its /assets/CoursesPDF/master-in-horticultural-science_admission-information_en_GB.pdf resolves (HTTP 200) but is an EMPTY shell containing only the unibz Advisory Service contact block; there is no unibz application portal entry, no unibz Early Bird / Late Application window, no unibz ranking list, no unibz EUR 50 non-EU application fee and no unibz selection score for this programme. Every unibz admission rule that applies to its other masters is IRRELEVANT here. WHAT UNIBO OPERATES: '(1) Access to the second cycle degree programme in International Horticultural Science - IMaHS is open, i.e., there is no maximum number of enrolments in A.Y. 2026/27. However, it is only possible to enrol in the programme if you meet the requirements set out in this notice and pass the verification of your personal competencies and skills conducted by a special Committee.' SO THERE IS NO RANKING AND NO CAP, BUT THERE IS A PASS/FAIL GATE with four cumulative components: (1) the required first-cycle qualification; (2) specific curricular requirements (degree class or 20 ECTS across four named subject groups); (3) English at CEFR B2; (4) 'adequate personal competencies and skills, verified according to the criteria specified by the programme'. NO TOLC, NO SAT, NO GRE/GMAT REQUIRED FOR ADMISSION (GRE is required only for the separate International Talents scholarship), NO PORTFOLIO, NO MOTIVATION LETTER, NO WRITTEN ENTRANCE TEST, NO SCORED RUBRIC AND NO CUT-OFF SCORE. The only assessment event is an online oral examination, from which only a narrow group of Italian graduates is exempt. APPLICATION CHANNEL: unibo's Studenti Online portal at https://studenti.unibo.it — 'Click on "Admission application", select "Second Cycle Degree Programme" and select the programme named "INTERNATIONAL HORTICULTURAL SCIENCE - IMAHS"'. Applicants resident abroad without an Italian identity document register via 'Register' then 'International student registration' to obtain a unibo username and password (SPID/CIE are not available to them). RE-APPLICATION IS ALLOWED: 'Those who participate in an intake and are not admitted to the programme may participate in subsequent intakes.'
academic_requirements: THREE STACKED REQUIREMENTS: a qualification, curricular credits, and a personal-competencies check. All three are set by the University of Bologna. 1) QUALIFICATION (Section 4.1 of the 2026/27 admission notice), verbatim: 'First cycle academic qualification: three-year university diploma or degree' OR 'Qualification obtained abroad recognised as suitable under Italian law, current international agreements and the rules laid down in the MUR Circular "Procedures for entry, residency and enrolment of international students and the respective recognition of qualifications for higher education courses in Italy" for A.Y. 2026/2027, published on www.universitaly.it/studenti-stranieri. The qualification must give access to a degree programme similar to that for which the candidate applies in Italy in the universities of the country of issuance.' You may apply before graduating. 2) CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS (Section 4.2), verbatim: 'students must hold a first cycle Degree, or a three-year university Degree, or other qualification obtained abroad, recognised as equivalent. Moreover, students must meet the following curricular requirements: a) holding the first cycle Degree in one of the following fields: Pursuant to Italian Min. Decree 270/04: L-25 Agricultural and forestry science; L-26 Food Science; L-2 Biotechnology; L-32 Environmental Sciences; L-13 Biological Sciences. Pursuant to Italian Min. Decree 509/99: Degree in Agricultural Science. Three-year university Degree: students must hold a first cycle University Degree in Life Sciences (e.g., Horticulture, Agriculture, Biology) obtained upon achievement of at least 180 ECTS. b) holding a first cycle Degree in a field other than the ones listed above and having acquired ECTS in the following subject groups: - AGR/01 - Agricultural economics and rural appraisal: 5 ECTS / CFU; - AGR/03 - Arboriculture and fruitculture: 5 ECTS / CFU; - AGR/11 - General and applied entomology: 5 ECTS / CFU; - AGR/12 - Plant pathology: 5 ECTS / CFU.' (i.e. 20 ECTS total across the four groups.) HOW A FOREIGN DEGREE IS HANDLED, verbatim from the programme's how-to-enrol page: 'The Committee assesses correspondence of the foreign qualification with the Italian qualification. In the absence of such correspondence, the Committee will assess the career in order to verify possession of a number of credits corresponding to the 20 University Educational Credits in the subject group indicated in the call.' So a foreign transcript is first mapped onto L-25/L-26/L-2/L-32/L-13, and only if that mapping fails is the 5+5+5+5 grid applied. SSD CODE NOTE (2024 reform): the admission notice still uses the OLD codes. Under the reformed nomenclature used in unibo's own 2026/27 course structure diagram the equivalents are AGR/01 -> AGRI-01/A (agricultural economics and rural appraisal); AGR/03 -> AGRI-03/A (arboriculture and fruitculture); AGR/11 -> AGRI-05/A (general and applied entomology); AGR/12 -> AGRI-05/B (plant pathology). [uncertain] unibo does not publish this old-to-new mapping alongside the admission notice; the mapping above is inferred from the SSDs attached to the corresponding taught courses in the 2026/27 diagram. HARD CONSEQUENCE: 'If you do not meet all the curricular requirements indicated, you will not be able to register for the programme.' There is no OFA, no credit debt and no conditional make-up route — gaps must be closed BEFORE applying, typically by taking Italian 'corsi singoli' (single supplementary courses) or equivalent courses elsewhere. 3) ADEQUATE PERSONAL COMPETENCIES AND SKILLS (Sections 4.4 and 6.2), verbatim: 'Personal competences and skills are met if the student graduated in classes L-25 or L-26 (Ministerial Decree 270/04) or L-20 (Ministerial Decree 509/99) with a grade equal to or higher than 100/110, or foreign equivalent. Otherwise, to prove the adequacy of your personal competencies and skills, you will have to take an oral examination which will be held online.' NOTE THERE IS NO GENERAL MINIMUM GPA — unlike unibz's own masters (which set floors such as 22/30), unibo sets no minimum average here; the 100/110 figure is only the threshold that EXEMPTS an Italian L-25/L-26/L-20 graduate from the oral exam. 4) GRADUATING APPLICANTS: 'You can apply even if you have not yet obtained your first cycle degree... In case of admission and subsequent enrolment, the degree must in any case be obtained by 31/12/2026; otherwise, any registration will be cancelled.' PRACTICAL READING FOR A TURKISH APPLICANT: a Turkish 4-year Ziraat Muhendisligi (Bahce Bitkileri, Bitki Koruma, Tarim Ekonomisi, Tarimsal Biyoteknoloji, Toprak Bilimi), Bahce Bitkileri, Bitki Koruma or Tarimsal Biyoteknoloji lisans normally maps cleanly onto L-25 and satisfies route (a) plus the 5+5+5+5 grid. Biyoloji, Moleküler Biyoloji ve Genetik and Cevre Muhendisligi degrees map onto L-13/L-32/L-2 and are formally admissible, but candidates from those programmes should still expect the oral exam because they will almost certainly lack arboriculture and applied entomology coursework. Gida Muhendisligi maps to L-26. Note also that a Turkish 4-year degree is longer than the Italian 3-year first cycle, which is not a problem — the requirement is a MINIMUM of 180 ECTS.
entry_exam_or_test: ONE ASSESSMENT EVENT ONLY: AN ONLINE ORAL EXAMINATION. There is no written test of any kind. NOT REQUIRED: no TOLC (any variant), no CENT-S, no unibz admission test (unibz runs none for this programme), no SAT, no GMAT, no IELTS/TOEFL-as-a-test (a certificate is accepted, not a sitting), no portfolio, no video presentation, no motivation letter, no written entrance exam. GRE is NOT required for admission — it is required only if the applicant separately competes for the International Talents @Unibo scholarship. THE ORAL EXAMINATION, verbatim: 'the adequacy of personal competencies and skills will be assessed through an oral interview aimed at ascertaining academic knowledge of: economics and rural appraisal; arboriculture and fruitculture; general and applied entomology; plant pathology.' It is 'held online'. WHO SITS IT: everybody EXCEPT a candidate who 'graduated in classes L-25 or L-26 (Ministerial Decree 270/04) or L-20 (Ministerial Decree 509/99) with a grade equal to or higher than 100/110, or foreign equivalent'. Because those are Italian degree classes, a foreign-qualified applicant will in practice be called unless the Committee accepts a foreign equivalent of that 100/110 mark. The notice reinforces this: 'The requirements and documentation submitted during the application phase will be assessed by the Committee, which will determine whether further verification of your personal competencies and skills is necessary, if you hold a foreign qualification. If so, you will be called for an interview, which will take place in online mode on the date and according to the procedures indicated in the call itself.' OUTCOME LABELS PUBLISHED ON STUDENTI ONLINE: 'Admitted' (may register), 'Application submitted' (must take the test), 'Not admitted'. FAILURE CONSEQUENCE, verbatim: 'If you do not pass the oral interview, your personal competencies and skill will be deemed unsuitable and you will not be able to register for the programme. Those who participate in an intake and are not admitted to the programme may participate in subsequent intakes.' — so a failed oral in Intake 1 can be re-attempted in Intake 2 (and, for EU citizens, Intakes 3 and 4). DISABILITY/SLD ADAPTATIONS ARE AVAILABLE FOR THIS ORAL: extra time of 30% (SLD, other developmental disorders, specific medical conditions) or 50% (certified disability under Law 104/92), plus assistive tools; the request form and medical documentation must be uploaded on Studenti Online 'by the intake registration deadline'. Candidates residing abroad 'must submit legalized certifications (or with an Apostille where applicable) issued in their country of residence... accompanied by an official translation into Italian or English'. Contact: ases.adattamentiammissione@unibo.it. SEPARATELY, THE ENGLISH B2 REQUIREMENT is satisfied by certificate, native-speaker status or a prior B2 exam at unibo/an AICLU language centre — there is no unibo English entrance test to sit for this programme.
selection_scoring: THERE IS NO SCORED SELECTION RUBRIC, NO POINTS SYSTEM, NO CUT-OFF SCORE AND NO RANKING LIST — this is the structural difference from every unibz-run master. Because access is open ('there is no maximum number of enrolments in A.Y. 2026/27'), candidates are NOT ranked against one another and no threshold score is published. The assessment is purely PASS/FAIL against fixed criteria. THE ONLY NUMERIC THRESHOLD ANYWHERE IN THE PROCEDURE is the exemption bar for the oral exam: an Italian first-cycle degree in class L-25 or L-26 (M.D. 270/04) or L-20 (M.D. 509/99) 'with a grade equal to or higher than 100/110, or the foreign equivalent'. Below that mark — or with any qualification outside those classes — the candidate must pass the oral exam. There is no minimum GPA, no minimum weighted average and no minimum final mark for admission as such. THE EVALUATION COMMITTEE, named in full in the 2026/27 notice: 'prof. Francesco Spinelli (Chairman); prof. Massimo Tagliavini (Member); prof. Carlo Andreotti (Member); prof. Sania Barjc (Member); prof. Giuseppina Pennisi (Member); prof. Maria Luisa Dindo (Member); prof. Elena Baraldi (Member); prof. Antonella Samoggia (Member); prof. Giulia Maesano (Member); prof. Sergio Angeli (Secretary). All the professors who hold course units in the second cycle degree programme are also substitute members.' Note that Massimo Tagliavini, Carlo Andreotti and Sergio Angeli are unibz professors — the Bolzano side sits on the unibo admission committee, which is the clearest procedural sign of the genuinely joint governance of the programme. WHAT THE COMMITTEE ACTUALLY DOES: 'A committee will check the candidates' personal competencies and skills and that they meet the requirements for admission' — i.e. it verifies the qualification, maps the foreign transcript onto the Italian degree classes or the 20-ECTS grid, checks the English B2 evidence, and decides whether an oral is needed. KNOCK-OUT PROCEDURAL RULE, verbatim: 'The committee will only assess documents uploaded through the Studenti Online application (www.studenti.unibo.it). Any mandatory documents that are missing or only partially uploaded by the application deadline shall result in the candidate not being considered. Documents must not be sent by post or email to the administrative offices.' FALSE-DECLARATION PENALTY: 'In the event of false declarations, in addition to incurring the penalties laid down in Article 496 of the Italian Criminal Code, you will automatically forfeit your right to registration and any benefits obtained, without being entitled to any reimbursement of the sums paid.' [uncertain] No pass mark, grading scale, duration or structure is published for the oral examination itself, and no statistics on pass/fail rates or on how many candidates apply per intake are published by unibo for this programme.
bonus_points: NO BONUS POINTS EXIST — because there is no scored ranking at all. Specifically, and in contrast to unibz's own masters: there is NO Webometrics university-ranking bonus (that is unibz's Master in Software Engineering and Master in Computing for Data Science, 3/2/1 points for a bachelor from a top-1000/1001-2000/2001-3000 university); NO GMAT/GRE admission bonus (unibz's Master in Accounting and Finance); NO startup-project bonus (unibz's Master in Entrepreneurship and Innovation); NO points for English above B2 (unibz's Master in Energy Engineering awards up to 10); and NO video-presentation points. B2 English is a binary gate here — a C1 or C2 certificate confers no admission advantage whatsoever. THE ONLY PLACE WHERE MERIT IS SCORED IS IN SCHOLARSHIP COMPETITIONS, NOT IN ADMISSION: (1) the DISTAL call for 4 IMaHS scholarships of EUR 1,500 gross for the third semester at unibz is decided on 'merit' evidenced by 'autocertificazione degli esami sostenuti con voti' (self-certification of exams taken with grades) — but it is open only to students ALREADY enrolled in the first year, so it cannot help an applicant; (2) the International Talents @Unibo scholarship requires a GRE score sent to unibo with institution code 7850 and applies an age limit and an ISEE band. PRACTICAL IMPLICATION: an applicant should spend zero effort on score-maximising and all effort on (a) documenting the four AGR subject groups convincingly with syllabi, and (b) preparing technically for the oral exam.
portfolio_and_materials: NO PORTFOLIO, NO VIDEO, NO PROJECT PROPOSAL AND NO MOTIVATION LETTER. There is one programme-specific form and a short set of transcript documents. MANDATORY UPLOADS (all in PDF, all through Studenti Online, all within the intake window): (1) 'front and back copy of a valid identity document' — and, verbatim, 'If you are a citizen of a foreign country and your identity document does not have an English translation: copy of your passport'. For Turkish applicants this means uploading the passport, since the Turkish kimlik card is not in English. (2) THE QUALIFICATION EVIDENCE, differentiated by origin. unibo graduates/graduands: select the system-generated self-certification of their unibo career (no signature required). Other Italian universities: 'self-certification of your first cycle academic qualification with a list of exams taken. If you have not yet obtained your qualification, upload a self-certification of the exams taken'. Foreign qualifications, verbatim: 'a copy of the qualification obtained abroad, translated into Italian or English, allowing access to second cycle degree programmes the country where it was obtained (or in the country of reference for the system), accompanied by a transcript of records and Diploma Supplement where available. If you have not yet obtained the qualification, upload the list of exams taken (Transcript of Records).' (3) 'Proof of B2 level of knowledge of the English language'. (4) 'Imahs application form, filled in and signed' — a programme-specific form that is a HARD requirement and is easy to overlook; it is downloaded from the programme's how-to-enrol page / the Studenti Online application. (5) COURSE-UNIT DATA ENTERED IN THE FORM, not uploaded: 'if you obtained your qualification from another Italian university or abroad: enter the details of the course units you passed'. unibo graduates are exempt ('you do not need to upload information already held by the University'). OPTIONAL UPLOADS: 'A copy of a valid residence permit, if already held'; and the 'Form for requesting adaptations for persons with disabilities'. AT MATRICULATION (a later and separate step): a .jpg passport-size photo of the face; and, for foreign qualifications, the translated/legalised originals uploaded under the Studenti Online 'Calls' item 'Matriculation for A.Y. 26_27 - document upload for international students with foreign qualifications', followed by an in-person appointment with the International Student Administration Office in Bologna to show originals. FORMAT LIMITS: unibo publishes no page limit, MB cap or character limit for any of these documents — there is nothing analogous to unibz's 20 MB portfolio cap or 6,000-character motivation letter. The only format rules are 'in PDF' and 'translated into Italian or English'. STRATEGIC ADVICE: because the Committee's real task is mapping your transcript onto AGR/01, AGR/03, AGR/11 and AGR/12, the highest-value optional material is detailed course syllabi (content, hours, credits) for the arboriculture, entomology, plant-pathology and agricultural-economics courses you took. The notice's general clause allows the Committee to assess 'the career' where direct class correspondence is absent, so a well-documented transcript is worth more than any presentation material.
interview: YES — an ONLINE ORAL EXAMINATION is the central assessment of the whole procedure, and for a foreign-qualified applicant it should be treated as certain rather than conditional. SUBJECT MATTER, verbatim: 'an oral interview aimed at ascertaining academic knowledge of: economics and rural appraisal; arboriculture and fruitculture; general and applied entomology; plant pathology.' The how-to-enrol page words it as: 'A specific Committee assesses the basic academic knowledge of Agricultural economics and rural appraisal, Arboriculture and fruitculture, General and applied entomology, Plant Pathology, through an oral examination.' Note the four subjects are exactly the four AGR subject groups of the curricular requirement — the oral is essentially a live verification that the 5+5+5+5 ECTS were really learned. FORMAT: 'held online'. Conducted by the named Evaluation Committee chaired by Prof. Francesco Spinelli. WHO IS EXEMPT: only holders of an Italian first-cycle degree in class L-25 or L-26 (M.D. 270/04) or L-20 (M.D. 509/99) with a final mark of at least 100/110 'or foreign equivalent'. WHO IS EFFECTIVELY GUARANTEED TO SIT IT: holders of a foreign qualification. Verbatim: 'The requirements and documentation submitted during the application phase will be assessed by the Committee, which will determine whether further verification of your personal competencies and skills is necessary, if you hold a foreign qualification. If so, you will be called for an interview.' SCHEDULING, verbatim from all four intake schedules: 'IF CALLED FOR AN INTERVIEW: Interview dates (Section 4.4.b) - The date of the interview will be communicated by email sent to your institutional email address.' The institutional address is name.surname@studio.unibo.it, created automatically at registration — a candidate who never checks it will simply miss the convocation. The interview necessarily falls between the intake's closing date and its results date, i.e. for 2026/27: Intake 1 between 28/02 and 30/03/2026; Intake 2 between 10/05 and 08/06/2026; Intake 3 between 23/08 and 14/09/2026; Intake 4 between 25/10 and 09/11/2026. FAILURE: 'If you do not pass the oral interview, your personal competencies and skill will be deemed unsuitable and you will not be able to register for the programme' — but re-application in a later intake is allowed. [uncertain] No fixed interview dates, no duration, no pass mark, no indicative reading list and no sample questions are published anywhere on unibo.it or unibz.it for this programme. Candidates are convoked individually.
conditional_admission: YES — applying and even MATRICULATING before graduating is expressly permitted, with one hard cut-off date. APPLYING BEFORE GRADUATION, verbatim: 'You can apply even if you have not yet obtained your first cycle degree (see Section 4.1).' Not-yet-graduated applicants upload a Transcript of Records / list of exams taken instead of the diploma. THE HARD DEADLINE, verbatim: 'In case of admission and subsequent enrolment, the degree must in any case be obtained by 31/12/2026; otherwise, any registration will be cancelled.' Repeated at Section 7.1.a: 'If you have not yet graduated at the time of matriculation, you must obtain your degree by 31 December 2026 at the latest. Otherwise, your matriculation will be cancelled.' And on the how-to-enrol page: 'if you do not graduate by 31 December 2026, you will not be able to participate in the selection procedure and finalise your enrolment.' NOTE: THERE IS NO MINIMUM-ECTS CONDITION TO APPLY WHILE STILL STUDYING. Unlike unibz masters (which typically require 120 ECTS already earned, or 140 for Data Analytics), unibo sets no credit floor here — the only condition is finishing by 31/12/2026. [uncertain] DISCREPANCY FOUND: one block of the programme's how-to-enrol page states 'the qualification must be obtained by 31 December 2027; otherwise, your enrolment will be cancelled', while every other occurrence on the same page and the whole admission notice say 31 December 2026. This looks like an un-updated fragment on the web page. The signed admission notice (31/12/2026) is the authoritative text and should be assumed binding; do not rely on the 2027 date. A SECOND, SEPARATE FORM OF PROVISIONAL STATUS applies to foreign qualifications regardless of graduation: admission and pre-enrolment validation are provisional until the International Student Administration Office verifies the qualification's eligibility and the documents' authenticity, which happens ONLY after the first instalment is paid and originals are shown in person. Verbatim warning: 'If you hold a foreign qualification, admission to the programme and, where applicable, any subsequent conditional or unconditional validation of your pre-enrolment by the University do not automatically grant you the right to complete your matriculation or activate your student career. This applies even if you have obtained an entry visa, are physically present in Italy, or are eligible for, or receiving, scholarships or other grants.' CAREER ACTIVATION DEADLINE: 'Career activation must take place by 26 February 2027; otherwise, your matriculation will be cancelled.' Career activation is what unlocks study plans, exam booking, Wi-Fi and library access.
ofa_rules: NOT APPLICABLE — and structurally impossible for this programme. OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning requirements) is an Italian instrument reserved for FIRST-CYCLE (bachelor) programmes: a student who fails a compulsory entrance test is admitted anyway but carries a remedial obligation. Italian law does not allow a second-cycle (laurea magistrale) student to enrol carrying curricular credit debts. For IMaHS this means the curricular gap must be closed BEFORE admission, not after: 'If you do not meet all the curricular requirements indicated, you will not be able to register for the programme.' The standard Italian remedy is to earn the missing AGR/01, AGR/03, AGR/11 or AGR/12 credits as 'corsi singoli' (single supplementary courses) at an Italian university, or equivalent courses abroad, and then apply in a later intake. Neither the 2026/27 admission notice, the how-to-enrol page, the course structure diagram nor any unibz page mentions OFA, additional learning requirements, remedial obligations or credit debts for this programme. The functional equivalents of OFA here, all applied at the gate rather than after enrolment, are: the 20-ECTS curricular grid, the oral examination on the four AGR subjects, and the English B2 gate.
language_requirements: ONE REQUIREMENT ONLY: ENGLISH AT CEFR B2. Verbatim: 'English language skills are required to at least CEFR level B2.' There is NO Italian requirement, NO German requirement, NO third language, NO entry level in any second language and NO exit/graduation language requirement. This is the simplest language profile of any programme in the unibz orbit. THREE WAYS TO SATISFY IT, verbatim from the programme page: 'The assessment of the B2 level knowledge and skills of English language is fulfilled if the candidate: - is a citizen of a country whose official language is English; - holds an official certification attesting English language knowledge at least at level B2; - has passed an English language exam of B2 level in the previous Degree Programme at the University of Bologna or at another University Language Centre part of the AICLU (Italian Association of University Language Centres).' The admission notice adds a fourth wording: 'being a native speaker'. TIMING: 'The English language requirement is fulfilled during the application phase' — the proof must be uploaded with the application, inside the intake window. There is no later window and no unibo English test to sit as a fallback for this programme. IMPORTANT ASYMMETRY WITH UNIBZ PRACTICE: unibz would normally recognise an English-medium bachelor as proof of English (and even count it as C1). unibo's IMaHS list does NOT include 'degree taught in English' as an accepted route — the three accepted routes are citizenship of an English-speaking country, an official certificate, or a B2 exam passed at unibo/an AICLU centre. [uncertain] Whether the Committee would in practice accept a medium-of-instruction letter from a fully English-taught foreign bachelor is not stated; the safe course for a Turkish applicant from an English-medium programme (METU, Bogazici, ITU English track, Bilkent, Koc, Sabanci) is to obtain an IELTS/TOEFL certificate rather than rely on the medium of instruction. ITALIAN LANGUAGE — EXPLICITLY NOT REQUIRED. unibo requires non-EU citizens residing abroad to prove Italian at B2 (unibo test min. 48/72, or CELI/CILS/PLIDA/CERTIT) only for programmes taught in Italian; 'This requirement does not apply to students enrolling in English-taught programs'. IMaHS is English-taught, so the Italian requirement and its 19/11/2026 deadline do not bite. GERMAN — NOT REQUIRED even for the Bolzano semester. unibz's trilingual C1/C1/B1 graduation model does not apply, because the student remains a University of Bologna student and the degree's language regime is unibo's.
entry_levels_by_position: ENGLISH B2 / none / none — a single teaching language in first position at B2, with no second or third language at any stage. unibz expresses language requirements by POSITION (1st/2nd/3rd teaching language) rather than by named language, and by that notation this programme is B2 / - / -. But note the notation is borrowed: the language rules here are set by the UNIVERSITY OF BOLOGNA, not by unibz, so unibz's positional framework does not formally govern the programme at all. COMPARISON TO PLACE IT: unibz's trilingual bachelors run B2/B2/none (Computer Science) or B2/B1/none (Electronic and Information Engineering); unibz's trilingual masters in Economics run C1/B2/none (Public Policy and Innovative Governance, Accounting and Finance); unibz's English-only masters run B2/none/none (Energy Engineering). IMaHS sits in the last, most accessible group — but with an additional advantage the unibz English-only masters do not have: no exposure at all to unibz's language-certificate rulebook, since compliance is judged against unibo's shorter list. ONE PRACTICAL NUANCE: unibz's own recognised-certificate list (University Council Resolution 16/2026) is IRRELEVANT here. A certificate that unibz would reject (for example a 'home edition' exam not on unibz's asterisked list) may still be accepted by unibo, and vice versa. Always check the unibo IMaHS list, not the unibz one.
exit_levels: NO EXIT / GRADUATION LANGUAGE REQUIREMENT AT ALL. unibz's C1/C1/B1 graduation model applies only to unibz's own TRILINGUAL programmes, and unibz's English-taught masters carry no additional language obligation. Neither model applies here anyway, because the student is enrolled at and graduates from the University of Bologna: the degree is awarded under unibo's rules, and unibo attaches no language exit requirement to this programme. The 2026/27 admission notice's language section (4.3) covers ENTRY ONLY and is one sentence long. The course structure diagram contains an activity type 'E: Final examination and foreign language test' as a generic unibo category label, but no foreign-language test appears among the programme's actual activities — the E-type items are the thesis and internship options only. PRACTICAL SIGNIFICANCE: this removes the classic hidden risk of studying in Bolzano. In unibz's trilingual programmes students routinely gain admission and then cannot graduate on time because they have not certified the second and third languages. Here, once admitted with B2 English, no further language certification stands between the student and the joint degree. Voluntary language study is still worth doing — Italian for daily life and internships in Bologna, German for the South Tyrolean fruit and wine industry, which is the programme's main employment catchment — but it carries no graduation consequence.
third_language_exam_threshold: NOT APPLICABLE — there is no second language, therefore no third language and no third-language B1 threshold. The rule this field exists to capture (unibz's requirement of B1 in the third language before a student may sit exams from the second semester of the first year onward) belongs exclusively to unibz's TRILINGUAL programmes and cannot apply to a programme that is 'entirely taught and assessed in English' and administered by the University of Bologna. There is likewise no first- or second-language exam threshold gating exam attendance, no annual language progress check and no Language Centre obligation. The only language condition attached to IMaHS is the English B2 gate, which is settled at the application stage and never revisited.
proof_pathways: THREE ACCEPTED ROUTES (unibo's list for this programme — narrower than unibz's four-route model): (1) CITIZENSHIP OF AN ENGLISH-SPEAKING COUNTRY — 'is a citizen of a country whose official language is English'; the admission notice also phrases this as 'being a native speaker'. (2) AN OFFICIAL CERTIFICATE AT B2 OR ABOVE from the published list, subject to the validity rule below. (3) A B2 ENGLISH EXAM ALREADY PASSED at the University of Bologna or at another Italian university language centre belonging to AICLU — evidenced by 'autocertificazione scaricabile da Studenti Online' / 'self-certification downloadable from Studenti Online including passing the ENGLISH LANGUAGE B-2 (or higher) test in a previous career at the University of Bologna or at the Free University of Bolzano'. Note this route explicitly names the FREE UNIVERSITY OF BOLZANO language centre alongside unibo's CLA — useful for anyone who previously studied at unibz. TIMING AND CHANNEL: the proof is uploaded as a PDF with the application on Studenti Online, inside the intake window. There is no separate language-exam registration period and no unibo English test offered as a fallback for this programme (unlike unibz, which runs Language Centre exam sittings for its own applicants). WHAT IS NOT ON THE LIST: 'a bachelor or master degree taught in English' is NOT listed as an accepted route for IMaHS, even though unibo accepts it for some other programmes and unibz accepts it for all of its own. [uncertain] The Committee's practice on medium-of-instruction letters is not published. For a Turkish applicant, the operational recommendation is therefore: obtain an IELTS Academic (5.5+) or TOEFL iBT (80+) certificate dated after 01/01/2023, and treat any medium-of-instruction letter as a supporting extra, not as the primary proof. PRE-ENROLMENT LINKAGE: for non-EU applicants the language certificate is also one of the documents to bring to the Italian Embassy/Consulate for the visa appointment — unibo lists 'any certificates relating to the degree programme's language requirement' among the visa-appointment documents.
certificate_rules: GOVERNED BY UNIBO'S PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC LIST, NOT BY UNIBZ'S RULEBOOK. unibz's University Council Resolution 16/2026 (five-year validity, four skills, lowest sub-skill determines the level, no compensation, DAAD not recognised, restricted 'home edition' acceptance) DOES NOT APPLY to this programme. VALIDITY RULE, verbatim: 'The recognised English language certifications are the following, obtained after 01/01/2023'. This is a fixed cut-off date, not a rolling five-year window — a certificate issued on or before 31/12/2022 is not accepted regardless of age. [uncertain] This date appears on the live programme page as consulted on 2026-08-29 and is presumably rolled forward each cycle; a 2027/28 applicant should re-check it rather than assume 01/01/2023 still applies. THE FULL RECOGNISED LIST FOR IMaHS, with the minimum scores exactly as published: British Council / IDP / Cambridge Assessment English - IELTS (Academic), minimum 5.5/9; British Council / IDP / Cambridge Assessment English - IELTS (General Training), minimum 5.5/9 (note: General Training is accepted, which is unusual and helpful); Educational Testing Service (ETS) - TOEFL iBT, minimum 80; Cambridge Assessment English - Cambridge English Preliminary (PET), minimum 160 / pass with Distinction; Cambridge Assessment English - Cambridge B1 Preliminary, minimum 160 / grade A; Cambridge Assessment English - Cambridge English First (FCE), minimum 160 / grade C; Cambridge Assessment English - Cambridge B2 First, minimum 160 / grade C; Cambridge Assessment English - Cambridge English Advanced (CAE) [no minimum stated]; Cambridge Assessment English - Cambridge C1 Advanced, minimum 180; Cambridge Assessment English - Cambridge English Proficiency (CPE) [no minimum stated]; Cambridge Assessment English - Cambridge C2 Proficiency, minimum 200; Cambridge Assessment English - Cambridge B2 Business Vantage (BEC Vantage), minimum 160 / grade C; Cambridge Assessment English - Cambridge C1 Business Higher (BEC Higher), minimum 180; Trinity College London - ISE II, III, IV; Cambridge Assessment International Education - IGCSE English as a Second Language, minimum grade C; Cambridge Assessment International Education - IGCSE First Language English, minimum grade C; University of Bologna Language Centre (CLA) and Free University of Bolzano Language Centre - self-certification from Studenti Online of a passed B2 (or higher) English exam in a previous career. NOTES ON WHAT IS ABSENT FROM THIS LIST — and these absences matter: no PTE Academic, no Duolingo English Test, no TOEIC, no LanguageCert, no Aptis, no Michigan MET, no PEIC. Several of those ARE accepted by unibz for its own programmes, so a candidate holding, for example, a PTE Academic or a LanguageCert should not assume it will pass here. IELTS 5.5 AND TOEFL iBT 80 ARE STRIKINGLY LOW BARS by international-master standards (unibz's own English-taught masters accept IELTS 5.5-6.5 for B2, so the level is comparable, but many competing European agriculture masters demand IELTS 6.5). This is one of the genuinely easy parts of the application. [uncertain] unibo does not publish, for this programme, whether all four skills must be assessed, whether sub-skill minima apply, or whether at-home/online editions (TOEFL iBT Home Edition, IELTS Online) are accepted.
application_deadline_eu: FOUR INTAKES for A.Y. 2026/27, all closing at 13:00 (1 PM) Italian time on the closing day. Dates normalised to ISO; unibo writes DD/MM/YYYY. Intakes 3 and 4 are marked 'EU citizen applicants only'. INTAKE 1 — opens 2026-02-02, closes 2026-02-28 at 13:00; results published from 2026-03-30. Open to ALL applicants including non-EU residing abroad. INTAKE 2 — opens 2026-03-02, closes 2026-05-10 at 13:00; results published from 2026-06-08. Open to ALL applicants including non-EU residing abroad. This is the LAST intake a non-EU citizen residing abroad can use. INTAKE 3 (EU CITIZEN APPLICANTS ONLY) — opens 2026-05-11, closes 2026-08-23 at 13:00; results published from 2026-09-14. INTAKE 4 (EU CITIZEN APPLICANTS ONLY) — opens 2026-08-24, closes 2026-10-25 at 13:00; results published from 2026-11-09. NOTE THE OVERLAP: Intake 1 and Intake 2 run concurrently for most of February (Intake 2 opens 02/03/2026, one day after Intake 1 has already closed on 28/02 — in fact they abut rather than overlap). Intakes 2 and 3 overlap by one day at the changeover. MATRICULATION WINDOW IS IDENTICAL FOR ALL FOUR INTAKES: 'From 03/06/2026 to 19/11/2026 (with late payment fee from October 30, 2026 to November 19, 2026)'. So an Intake 1 candidate admitted on 30/03/2026 still cannot matriculate until 03/06/2026. RE-APPLICATION IS ALLOWED: 'Those who participate in an intake and are not admitted to the programme may participate in subsequent intakes.' A candidate who fails the oral in February can retry in May, August and October (the last two only if an EU citizen). STATUS ON 2026-08-29: Intakes 1, 2 and 3 are closed. INTAKE 4 IS OPEN NOW and closes 2026-10-25 at 13:00 — but only for EU citizens. [uncertain] The 2027/28 notice and its intake dates are not yet published. On the 2026/27 pattern, expect the notice around December 2026 and a first intake opening in early February 2027.
application_deadline_non_eu: NON-EU CITIZENS RESIDING ABROAD GET TWO INTAKES, NOT FOUR — and both are in the first half of the year. This is the single most important planning fact for a Turkish, Indian, Pakistani, Iranian or other non-EU applicant living outside Italy. USABLE WINDOWS FOR 2026/27: Intake 1, 2026-02-02 to 2026-02-28 at 13:00 (results from 2026-03-30); and Intake 2, 2026-03-02 to 2026-05-10 at 13:00 (results from 2026-06-08). CLOSED TO THEM: Intake 3 (11/05-23/08/2026) and Intake 4 (24/08-25/10/2026) are both headed 'EU citizen applicants only' in the admission notice. WHY THE RESTRICTION EXISTS: it is driven by the visa pipeline, not by academic capacity. A non-EU applicant must, after passing the assessment, pre-enrol on Universitaly, have that pre-enrolment validated by unibo (which requires the first instalment to be paid), then obtain a type-D study visa from the Italian Embassy or Consulate — a chain that cannot realistically complete between late August and the 21/09/2026 start of teaching. THE EXTRA STEP, verbatim from the notice: 'If you are a non-EU citizen and reside abroad, in compliance with the procedures defined by the Italian Ministry of University and Research in the Circular "Procedures for entry, residency and enrolment of international students and the respective recognition of qualifications for higher education courses in Italy" for A.Y. 2026/2027 published on www.universitaly.it/studenti-stranieri, in addition to following the steps required for admission to the degree programme, you will have to: pre-enrol on Universitaly and request an entry visa for study purposes.' PRE-ENROLMENT VALIDATION LOGIC, verbatim: 'If you have passed the assessment and paid the first instalment by the mandatory deadline set by the call, the offices will validate your pre-enrolment. Download the application summary and submit it to the Embassy or Consulate to apply for a visa.' And a specific August warning: 'The University of Bologna's offices could be closed for several days in August, during which pre-enrolments are not validated, so pre-enrolment validation times could be longer in August.' RECOMMENDED TARGET: Intake 1 (February), not Intake 2. Intake 1 results land on 30/03/2026, leaving roughly six months for pre-enrolment, instalment, visa appointment and travel; Intake 2 results land on 08/06/2026, and matriculation only opens 03/06/2026, which compresses the visa window into the summer consular bottleneck. STATUS ON 2026-08-29: BOTH non-EU windows for 2026/27 are closed. A non-EU applicant abroad must now target 2027/28.
parity_of_treatment: UNIBO USES A THREE-WAY CLASSIFICATION, and which box you fall into determines how many intakes you get, whether you need a visa, and how your fees are computed. The notice directs applicants to 'Check which case you fall into at www.unibo.it/whoareinternationalstudents'. THE THREE CATEGORIES flagged in the notice's blue 'International' boxes: '(1) Students with a foreign qualification, regardless of citizenship; (2) Non-EU citizens with EU equivalent status; (3) Non-EU citizens with residency abroad.' CATEGORY 2 — 'NON-EU CITIZENS WITH EU EQUIVALENT STATUS' — IS THE PARITY CATEGORY AND IS DECISIVE FOR TURKISH APPLICANTS ALREADY IN ITALY. Such applicants are treated as EU citizens: they may use all four intakes, they need no visa and no Universitaly pre-enrolment, and they enrol directly. The status rests on holding a qualifying Italian residence permit. Verbatim requirement at career activation: 'If you are a non-EU citizen with EU equivalent status, in order to activate your career you must submit a copy of your valid residence permit which grants EU equivalent status to the Student Administration Office responsible for your degree programme.' THE HARD WARNING, verbatim: 'Check very carefully, at www.unibo.it/whoareinternationalstudents what is meant by "non-EU students with equivalent status" and what types of residence permits allow for equivalence. Lack of EU equivalent status will prevent you from matriculating, even if you have been admitted and have paid the first instalment.' THE TRAP FOR STUDENT-PERMIT HOLDERS, verbatim: 'Remember that, if you are a non-EU citizen, hold a student residence permit and formally withdraw from studies at this or another university, you lose the requirements for residency in Italy, and therefore your residence permit will be revoked and you will lose your EU-equivalent status.' Repeated in Section 7.2: such a person 'must return to your country of origin and initiate the pre-enrolment procedures through Universitaly at the competent Italian diplomatic mission (Embassy/Consulate)'. Practical translation: a Turkish student currently on an Italian STUDENT permit should transfer or change programme rather than withdraw, or they lose parity and fall back into the two-intake, visa-dependent track. [uncertain] Unlike unibz, unibo's IMaHS notice does not itself enumerate which permit types confer equivalence (unibz lists work, family reasons, political or humanitarian asylum, and religious reasons, and excludes study and tourism). The unibo definition sits on a separate page and was not enumerated verbatim in the sources checked. Italian national law (art. 39(5), Legislative Decree 286/1998) is the same underlying basis for both universities, so the unibz enumeration is a reliable guide but is not the unibo text. EEA/SWISS/SAN MARINO: not enumerated in this notice, but under the same national rules citizens of Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and Vatican City are treated as EU citizens for university access.
places_quotas: NO PLACES, NO QUOTAS, NO NUMERUS CLAUSUS — this is an OPEN-ACCESS programme. Verbatim: 'Access to the second cycle degree programme in International Horticultural Science - IMaHS is open, i.e., there is no maximum number of enrolments in A.Y. 2026/27.' CONSEQUENCES: there is no EU place count, no non-EU place count, no Early Bird / Late split of places, no waiting list, no ranking list and no publication of admitted-candidate IDs. Every applicant who meets the qualification, curricular, language and personal-competencies requirements is admitted. Competition between candidates plays no role whatsoever. THIS IS A MAJOR STRUCTURAL ADVANTAGE over unibz's own masters, which run tightly capped ranking lists (e.g. unibz's Master in Energy Engineering admitted 20 EU + 10 non-EU in Early Bird 2026/27 with 15 non-EU candidates left on a waiting list). Here the only thing standing between a qualified applicant and a place is the oral examination. [uncertain] WHETHER A SEPARATE VISA 'CONTINGENTE' APPLIES. Italian universities normally declare, on Universitaly, a quota of places reserved for non-EU citizens residing abroad even for open-access programmes, and unused reserved places revert to EU candidates. No IMaHS-specific contingente figure was found on unibo.it, on the programme pages or in the admission notice, and the notice's flat statement that there is no maximum number of enrolments suggests none is applied in practice — but this could not be positively confirmed for 2026/27 and should be checked with internationaldesk@unibo.it before relying on it. [uncertain] ACTUAL COHORT SIZE IS NOT PUBLISHED. unibo does not publish enrolment or applicant statistics for this programme, and no ranking lists exist to count from. The only indirect signal of scale is the DISTAL scholarship call, which funds 4 merit scholarships per year for students moving to Bolzano for the third semester — consistent with a small cohort, but not evidence of its size. SCHOLARSHIP QUOTAS THAT DO EXIST (not admission quotas): 4 IMaHS third-semester scholarships per year; 30 International Talents @Unibo grants across all unibo second-cycle programmes.
ranking_and_enrolment_dates: NO RANKING LIST IS EVER PUBLISHED for this programme, because access is open. What unibo publishes instead is an individual RESULT per applicant. RESULTS PUBLICATION, verbatim: 'The results of your application will be published on Studenti Online (www.studenti.unibo.it) and sent to your institutional email address (name.surname@studio.unibo.it), as from the date indicated for each intake.' Three possible outcomes: 'Admitted' (may register); 'Application submitted' (must take the oral test); 'Not admitted'. RESULT DATES FOR 2026/27: Intake 1 from 2026-03-30; Intake 2 from 2026-06-08; Intake 3 from 2026-09-14; Intake 4 from 2026-11-09. required_documents: TWO DISTINCT DOCUMENT SETS: one for the ADMISSION APPLICATION, a second and heavier one for MATRICULATION with a foreign qualification. SET A — ADMISSION APPLICATION (uploaded as PDF on Studenti Online within the intake window). Compulsory: (1) 'front and back copy of a valid identity document' — plus, for foreign citizens whose ID has no English translation, 'copy of your passport'; (2) the qualification required for admission — for a foreign qualification: 'a copy of the qualification obtained abroad, translated into Italian or English, allowing access to second cycle degree programmes the country where it was obtained (or in the country of reference for the system), accompanied by a transcript of records and Diploma Supplement where available'; if not yet graduated, 'the list of exams taken (Transcript of Records)'; (3) 'Proof of B2 level of knowledge of the English language'; (4) 'Imahs application form, filled in and signed' — the programme-specific form, and a hard knock-out if omitted; (5) course-unit details of exams passed, ENTERED IN THE ONLINE FORM (not uploaded) by applicants from other Italian universities or from abroad. Optional: 'A copy of a valid residence permit, if already held'; the disability/SLD adaptation request form plus supporting medical documentation. KNOCK-OUT RULE: 'Any mandatory documents that are missing or only partially uploaded by the application deadline shall result in the candidate not being considered. Documents must not be sent by post or email to the administrative offices.' NOTE: THERE IS NO MANDATORY EXCEL STUDY-CAREER TEMPLATE. That is a unibz instrument (used in unibz's Energy Engineering and other masters, where a missing Excel file voids the application). unibo's equivalent here is the IMaHS application form plus the in-form course-unit entry. SET B — MATRICULATION WITH A FOREIGN QUALIFICATION (after admission, after paying the first instalment): the original qualification certificate, a full transcript of exams passed, and a document establishing the qualification's VALUE — see credential_recognition. These are uploaded on Studenti Online under 'Calls' > 'Matriculation for A.Y. 26_27 - document upload for international students with foreign qualifications', followed by an in-person appointment at the International Student Administration Office in Bologna (Via Marsala 49/A) to present ORIGINALS. Non-EU applicants also upload their entry visa; EU-equivalent-status holders upload their residence permit. AT MATRICULATION also required: a .jpg passport-size photo of the face, and (for minors) a signed parental-responsibility form. ALSO NEEDED IN PRACTICE FOR AN INTERNATIONAL STUDENT: an Italian tax code (codice fiscale) from the Agenzia delle Entrate or the consulate; health coverage (EHIC for EU students, or private insurance, or SSN registration at a minimum EUR 700/year for study-permit holders); and, for fee reduction, ISEE or foreign income/asset documentation filed through ER.GO.

The 2026/27 admission notice sets out the full application procedure (Section 5) with no mention of any fee, and Section 8 ('Fees and benefits') covers only tuition after matriculation. There is nothing equivalent to unibz's EUR 50 non-refundable application fee for non-EU citizens living abroad — that fee belongs to unibz's own application portal, which is not used for this programme. THE FIRST MONEY DUE IS THE FIRST TUITION INSTALMENT AT MATRICULATION, paid via PagoPA: 'Pay the first instalment of your tuition fees via the PagoPA platform, as indicated on Studenti Online.' The fixed element is EUR 157.04 (which includes the Emilia-Romagna regional right-to-study tax and the EUR 16 stamp duty) and is payable by everyone, including students entitled to full exemption from the variable element. For a non-EU applicant this payment is also the trigger that lets unibo validate the Universitaly pre-enrolment for the visa. [uncertain] Marked uncertain only as absence of evidence: no unibo page consulted states affirmatively 'there is no application fee'; the conclusion rests on the fee's complete absence from the admission notice and from the application instructions. Other incidental costs a candidate should budget: an English certificate (IELTS/TOEFL, roughly EUR 200-260 in Turkey), document translation and legalisation/apostille, CIMEA Statement of Comparability if used (a paid service, roughly EUR 200-300), and the visa fee at the Italian consulate.
tuition_or_fees_link: FEES ARE PAID TO THE UNIVERSITY OF BOLOGNA ONLY — there is no separate unibz tuition for the Bolzano semester. The DISTAL scholarship call states that to take part, students must 'comply with payment of the tuition fees at UNIBO', confirming a single fee stream for the whole joint degree. unibz's own fee model (about EUR 1,200/year in two instalments of EUR 600) is IRRELEVANT here. STRUCTURE, verbatim: 'The fee to be paid to enrol for a degree programme consists of a fixed element of EUR 157.04 and a variable element calculated according to the student's family's financial situation (ISEE) up to a maximum that varies according to the programme.' The EUR 157.04 fixed element comprises the Emilia-Romagna regional right-to-study tax (approximately EUR 140) plus EUR 16 stamp duty plus an insurance premium, and is due from everyone. MAXIMUM: IMaHS does not appear on unibo's list of second-cycle programmes with an increased maximum, so the STANDARD second-cycle ceiling applies. For A.Y. 2025/26 that ceiling was EUR 2,550.00 'al netto della Tassa regionale per il diritto allo studio, dell'imposta di bollo e del premio assicurativo' (i.e. on top of the EUR 157.04). Total worst case for 2025/26 was therefore roughly EUR 2,707 per year. [uncertain] The 2026/27 maximum-amounts table was not published at the time of checking (2026-08-29); expect a small inflation-linked increase. FULL EXEMPTION: students with an ISEE at or below EUR 27,000 pay only the EUR 157.04 fixed element. Between EUR 27,000 and the top band the variable element scales progressively. IF YOU DO NOT FILE AN ISEE YOU PAY THE MAXIMUM: 'If you do not submit an ISEE certificate, you will have to pay the full tuition fees relevant to your degree programme.' ISEE deadline for 2026/27: 30 October 2026 at 18:00, or 16 November 2026 at 18:00 with a EUR 100 late fee. 'The deadline is peremptory and no exceptions are ever allowed.' INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS WITH INCOME ONLY ABROAD cannot obtain an ordinary ISEE and must instead file foreign income and asset documentation through ER.GO's online 'User dossier' by 20 November 2026: family composition, employment, gross 2025 income, real estate in square metres, outstanding mortgages, movable assets and disability status, translated into Italian, with diplomatic authentication or apostille where signed by public officials, and converted to euros at the Bank of Italy's 2025 exchange rates. This is a substantial paperwork exercise but it is what unlocks the difference between roughly EUR 157 and roughly EUR 2,707 per year. REDUCED FLAT FEE FOR SOME NATIONALITIES (2026/27): citizens of 'particularly poor and developing countries' pay a flat EUR 600 + EUR 157.04 for a second-cycle first year; citizens of non-EU, non-OECD countries pay a flat EUR 1,200 + EUR 157.04. NEITHER APPLIES TO TURKEY, because Turkey is an OECD member and is not on the developing-countries list. A Turkish student must therefore go the ISEE / foreign-income-documentation route to reduce fees. INSTALMENTS when an ISEE is filed: first instalment EUR 157.04 by 24 September 2026; second instalment by 18 December 2026; third instalment by 15 March 2027. For open-access second-cycle programmes without an ISEE the master's payment date is 29 October 2026, with late payment allowed to 19 November 2026 with a surcharge. Eligibility thresholds: ISEE up to EUR 25,000 and ISPE up to EUR 50,000. Crucially, applications are open to students 'indipendentemente dallo Stato e dalla regione di provenienza' — regardless of country of origin. The scholarship package also carries access to subsidised university residences, catering and international mobility contributions. Applications go through https://servizionline.er-go.it/domande2/ , independently of the degree application: 'The application for ER.GO grants is independent of the degree programme application and enrolment procedures... calls have a peremptory deadline and no exceptions are ever allowed.' NOTE: the third semester is spent in Bolzano, outside Emilia-Romagna — [uncertain] how ER.GO treats a semester of mandatory mobility to another region for residence and benefit purposes is not addressed in the sources checked and should be raised with ER.GO before the second year. 2) INTERNATIONAL TALENTS @UNIBO — unibo's flagship scholarship for international master's students: 30 grants university-wide, EUR 6,500 gross per year PLUS full tuition-fee exemption for two academic years. Eligibility: a qualification from a non-Italian education system; a GRE score taken by the deadline and reported to unibo with institution code 7850; ISEE (or equivalent foreign financial status) between EUR 16,000 and EUR 35,000; and 'you must not be older than 30 years on the closing date'. Applications exclusively through Studenti Online. For 2025/26 the deadline was 30 May 2025 at 12:00 CEST with results in July. [uncertain] The 2026/27 call's exact deadline, grant count and amount were not directly verifiable — the unibo landing page returned 404 at the time of checking; a 2026/27 call is reported to exist with a 30 May 2026 deadline. THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST VALUABLE OPTION FOR A NON-EU APPLICANT and the only one requiring a GRE, so it must be planned months ahead. 3) THE PROGRAMME'S OWN IMaHS MOBILITY SCHOLARSHIP — DISTAL runs an annual call: 'Each year, the IMaHS degree programme board offers scholarships based on merit for second year students who will take the third semester at the Free University of Bozen.' For 2026/27: 4 scholarships of EUR 1,500 gross each, deadline 20 April 2026 at 13:00, applied for through Studenti Online, decided on merit evidenced by a self-certification of exams passed with grades; applicants must be first-year IMaHS students (2025-26 cohort) and must commit to spending the third semester at unibz and to being up to date with unibo tuition payments. This is a SECOND-YEAR benefit — it cannot help at the application stage, but it partly offsets the cost of the Bolzano move. 4) ERASMUS+ MOBILITY GRANTS — 'Students enrolled will have the opportunity to spend up to two semesters (2nd, 3rd or 4th) in one of the European partner universities as exchange students Erasmus+ (with financial assistance)': Szent Istvan University Budapest, TU Munich, BOKU Wien, Humboldt University Berlin.
