Applying for ER.GO and filing income documentation is worthwhile even before deciding to enrol.
credential_recognition: RECOGNITION IS HANDLED BY THE UNIVERSITY OF BOLOGNA, IN TWO STAGES, AND THE SECOND STAGE IS THE HARD ONE. STAGE 1 — AT ADMISSION (light touch): upload 'a copy of the qualification obtained abroad, translated into Italian or English, allowing access to second cycle degree programmes the country where it was obtained... accompanied by a transcript of records and Diploma Supplement where available'. The Committee assesses correspondence with the Italian degree classes or, failing that, with the 20-ECTS AGR grid, and 'Curricular requirements and personal competencies are verified using exam copies and syllabi on a case-by-case basis'. No legalisation is required at this stage. STAGE 2 — AT MATRICULATION (full formal recognition). Three categories of document are required: the original qualification certificate (translated, with authenticity confirmed); the original certificate listing all passed exams (translated); and a document establishing the qualification's VALUE. THE FOUR ACCEPTED 'VALUE' DOCUMENTS: (a) DECLARATION OF VALUE (Dichiarazione di Valore in Loco) issued by the Italian Embassy or Consulate in the country of award — the traditional route, stating institutional status, access requirements, duration and academic/professional value; (b) an ENIC-NARIC CERTIFICATE, with unibo explicitly naming the CIMEA Certificate/Statement of Comparability, the WES Equivalency Certificate (ICAP package) and the KMK Statement of Comparability, 'provided they contain assessment information typically found in declarations of value'; (c) for institutions in the European Higher Education Area, 'a signed Diploma Supplement compliant with European Commission standards', which for second-cycle enrolments 'may eliminate the need for exam transcripts'; (d) for Lisbon Convention countries, free correspondence certificates from the ARDI database, where available. TRANSLATION: documents in English, French or Spanish need NO translation; other languages require an Italian or English translation — outside Italy following Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs procedures, inside Italy via a sworn translator at a district court. LEGALISATION: documents require legalisation at the Italian Embassy OR an Apostille (Hague Convention countries) on the signatures of university representatives, public officials or notaries. EXEMPTIONS: no value documentation is needed for secondary diplomas from EU countries, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino or the United Kingdom. WHEN AND HOW: after admission and after paying the first instalment, upload everything on Studenti Online under 'Calls' > 'Matriculation A.Y. 26_27 - document upload for international students with foreign qualifications', then 'make an appointment with the International Student Administration Office in Bologna or on your campus in order to show the original copies of your documentation'. Verbatim warning: 'These checks are carried out by the International Student Administration Office... only after you have paid the first instalment of matriculation and submitted the original copies of all the required documentation.' SPECIFIC ROUTE FOR A TURKISH APPLICANT: Turkey is a Hague Apostille country and a Lisbon Recognition Convention party, and Turkish diplomas are in Turkish, so the practical package is (i) the lisans diploma and the transcript, (ii) a certified English or Italian translation, (iii) an Apostille (apostil) from the relevant Valilik/Kaymakamlik on the notarised documents, and (iv) EITHER a Declaration of Value from the Italian Consulate General in Istanbul or the Embassy in Ankara, OR — usually faster and more predictable — a CIMEA Statement of Comparability. If the Turkish university issues a European-standard Diploma Supplement in English, that can also serve. Turkish YOK-registered state and foundation universities are recognised institutions, so the substantive recognition is normally straightforward; the delay risk lies entirely in the apostille and consular appointment queue, which should be started months before matriculation. MINIMUM CREDITS: the qualification must evidence at least 180 ECTS and must give access to second-cycle programmes in the awarding country. A Turkish 4-year lisans (240 ECTS) satisfies both comfortably. FINAL WARNING, verbatim: 'If you have been admitted... admission to the programme and, where applicable, any subsequent conditional or unconditional validation of your pre-enrolment by the University do not automatically grant you the right to complete your matriculation or activate your student career. This applies even if you have obtained an entry visa, are physically present in Italy, or are eligible for, or receiving, scholarships or other grants.'
non_eu_visa_process: A SIX-STEP CHAIN, and every step has a dependency on the one before it. This is the University of Bologna's process, not unibz's. STEP 1 — APPLY AND PASS THE ASSESSMENT in Intake 1 or Intake 2 (the only intakes open to non-EU citizens residing abroad). STEP 2 — MATRICULATE AND PAY THE FIRST INSTALMENT on Studenti Online via PagoPA within the matriculation window (03/06/2026-19/11/2026 for 2026/27; the practical deadline is much earlier because of the visa). STEP 3 — PRE-ENROL ON UNIVERSITALY at https://www.universitaly.it/first-steps , naming this degree programme. Verbatim: 'After you have passed the assessment, if you have not already done so, submit the pre-enrolment application online on Universitaly. You will need this to apply for an entry visa. Please indicate this degree programme on your application.' unibo publishes a guide at https://www.unibo.it/en/attachments/guide-universitaly . STEP 4 — GET THE PRE-ENROLMENT VALIDATED BY UNIBO: 'If you have passed the assessment and paid the first instalment by the mandatory deadline set by the call, the offices will validate your pre-enrolment. Download the application summary and submit it to the Embassy or Consulate to apply for a visa.' If the consulate demands UNCONDITIONAL validation, the applicant must first submit the foreign-qualification documents to the International Student Administration Office and notify it by email. AUGUST WARNING: 'The University of Bologna's offices could be closed for several days in August, during which pre-enrolments are not validated.' STEP 5 — APPLY FOR THE TYPE-D 'STUDY - UNIVERSITY ENROLMENT' VISA at the Italian Embassy/Consulate, bringing: the unibo-validated Universitaly pre-enrolment summary; 'the document certifying the economic resources needed to stay in Italy (minimum required for 2025: EUR 7,000.97; For 2026, the amount is currently being defined)', for example a bank statement; certificates for the language requirement; health insurance; Agenzia delle Entrate forms for the Italian tax code; and the qualification documents for translation/legalisation where the consulate provides that service. [uncertain] the 2026 financial-means figure was still 'being defined' at the time of checking. NOTE how much lower this is than unibz's requirement for South Tyrol (unibz cites at least EUR 800/month and roughly EUR 24,000 total for a master) — the Italian national minimum applied by unibo is a single annual figure of about EUR 7,000. STEP 6 — AFTER ARRIVAL: apply for the residence permit (permesso di soggiorno) for study purposes; obtain the codice fiscale; and arrange health cover — either private insurance or voluntary registration with the Italian National Health Service at a minimum of EUR 700.00 per calendar year (EUR 2,000 for dependants), paid by F24 with region code 06, 'per calendar year only... not possible to pay reduced fees for shorter periods', so a September arrival usually pays for two calendar years at once. Then upload the visa and originals under the Studenti Online 'Calls' matriculation item and attend the in-person appointment at the International Student Administration Office, Via Marsala 49/A, Bologna. Finally, ACTIVATE THE CAREER by 26 February 2027. HARD WARNINGS, verbatim: 'Remember that pre-enrolment does guarantee admission to degree programmes. To enrol, you must also meet the admission requirements and pass the entrance exams required by the degree programme'; 'The University of Bologna does not issue letters of academic eligibility for the purpose of obtaining a visa'; 'An entry visa for tourism cannot be used for university enrolment or to obtain a residence permit for study purposes.' THE THIRD-SEMESTER MOVE TO BOLZANO does not change university or permit type — the student remains enrolled at unibo throughout — but it does mean a change of address, which must be reflected in the residence-permit and health-registration records. [uncertain] Neither unibo nor unibz publishes guidance on the permit/residency mechanics of the mandatory Bologna-to-Bolzano move; this should be raised with the International Student Administration Office before the second year. WORK RIGHTS: an Italian study residence permit allows part-time work up to 20 hours per week / 1,040 hours per year, under national law.

uncertainty_notes: WHAT IS FIRMLY ESTABLISHED (from the signed 2026/27 unibo admission notice and unibo's live 2026/27 pages): the external application routing to unibo; open access with no cap; the four intake windows and the EU-only restriction on Intakes 3 and 4; LM-69 (LM-69 R) and codes 6784/8883; the curricular requirements and the four AGR subject groups; English B2 and the exact certificate table; the online oral examination and its 100/110 exemption; the 31/12/2026 graduation deadline and the 26/02/2027 career-activation deadline; the fee architecture (EUR 157.04 fixed + ISEE-scaled variable); the joint-degree status; the full 2026/27 curriculum with per-course ECTS and campus split. PRINCIPAL UNCERTAINTIES AND CONFLICTS: (1) JOINT vs DOUBLE DEGREE. unibo says both things in different places: the admission notice and the programme overview say 'joint degree' / 'joint Degree recognized by both institutions', while the unibo central catalogue page adds that 'Graduates earn a double degree from both institutions', and the unibz brochure separately describes a DIFFERENT double degree earned through Erasmus+ partner universities. What the physical parchment(s) look like is not documented. (2) 31 DECEMBER 2026 vs 2027. One fragment of unibo's how-to-enrol page says the qualification must be obtained by 31 December 2027; the admission notice and every other occurrence say 31 December 2026. Treat 31/12/2026 as binding. (3) THE UNIBZ-SIDE MATERIAL IS STALE. The unibz brochure is headed '2017/18', the unibz page links a 2017 study plan and a 2017 timetable, unibz's admission-information PDF is an empty shell, and unibo's course diagram still calls the Bolzano host 'Faculty of Science and Technology' although unibz now files the programme under the Faculty of Agricultural, Environmental and Food Sciences. None of this affects the programme's active status, but it means unibz-side content must not be used for operational facts. (4) NO COMPETITIVENESS DATA AT ALL. No ranking lists, no applicant counts, no enrolment figures, no oral-exam pass rates, no cohort size. Open access means none of this is published. (5) SSD OLD-TO-NEW MAPPING (AGR/01->AGRI-01/A, AGR/03->AGRI-03/A, AGR/11->AGRI-05/A, AGR/12->AGRI-05/B) is INFERRED from the SSDs on the corresponding 2026/27 courses; unibo does not publish the mapping next to the admission notice. (6) 2026/27 MAXIMUM TUITION not yet published; the EUR 2,550.00 second-cycle ceiling quoted is the 2025/26 figure. (7) INTERNATIONAL TALENTS @UNIBO 2026/27 details (deadline, count, amount) are extrapolated from the 2025/26 call; the unibo landing page returned HTTP 404 when checked. (8) NO INTERVIEW DATES, no oral-exam duration, pass mark, format detail or reading list is published. (9) VISA FINANCIAL MEANS for 2026 was still 'being defined' (2025 figure: EUR 7,000.97). (10) NON-EU VISA 'CONTINGENTE': no reserved-places figure was found for this programme, and the notice's 'no maximum number of enrolments' implies none, but this could not be positively confirmed. (11) MEDIUM-OF-INSTRUCTION AS ENGLISH PROOF is not on unibo's accepted list for this programme; whether the Committee accepts it in practice is unknown. Get a certificate. (12) ER.GO TREATMENT OF THE MANDATORY BOLZANO SEMESTER (residence status, 'fuori sede' classification, benefit continuity) is not addressed in any source found. (13) DOUBLE-DEGREE MECHANICS with Budapest/Munich/BOKU Wien/Humboldt (selection, quotas, deadlines, language requirements) are not published. (14) RESIDENCE-PERMIT AND ADDRESS MECHANICS of the Bologna-to-Bolzano move for non-EU students are not documented by either university. (15) FIRST YEAR OF ACTIVATION unknown; course-structure archives reach back to 2010/2011. (16) 2027/28 CYCLE entirely unpublished — all dates in this record are 2026/27 and will change. DATA-SET WARNING: this programme must be flagged separately in any unibz data set. Applying unibz's standard fields to it produces systematically wrong answers — there is no unibz Early Bird/Late window, no unibz EUR 50 application fee, no unibz ranking list, no unibz selection score, no unibz language-certificate rulebook, no unibz EUR 1,200/year fee and no unibz South Tyrol provincial scholarship.
